Great project, but sales transparency needs improvement

The Positives:
1. Exceptional Construction Quality & Design: The project lives up to Shapoorji Pallonji’s reputation with robust construction, spacious layouts, and premium finishes like vitrified tiles, laminated doors, and branded fittings . The towers are well-planned, and the Goan-themed architecture adds a unique charm .

3. Top-Notch Amenities: The project offers 25+ amenities, including a swimming pool, gym, clubhouse, jogging track, and even a skating rink . The water treatment plant and solar facilities highlight sustainability efforts .

The Negatives (Sales Process Issues):
1.  Misleading Commitments by Sales Team : Our salesperson, **Mandeep Pandey**, made false promises:
Kitchen Trolley Assured it would be installed by the builder but wasn’t delivered.

- Hidden Charges - Claims like "free AC bus service, banquet hall, and mini-theatre included in maintenance" were untrue these incur extra costs . *Tip for buyers*: Negotiate to remove unwanted services (e.g., bus cost) from the cost sheet.

2. Pressure Tactics & Fake Urgency The team created artificial demand ("Last 4 flats left!") to rush decisions. Always verify availability independently and take time to evaluate .

3. Cash Payment Demand : The relationship manager Mr rakesh parekh insisted on ₹10,000 cash for "legal fees" during registration, refusing digital payment a red flag for transparency.

Final Verdict
Joyville Virar is a stellar project for its construction, amenities, and lifestyle . However, proceed cautiously with sales discussions
- Document all promises in writing.
- Scrutinize cost breakdowns for hidden charges.
- Avoid rushed decisions under pressure.

Recommendation : Ideal for families seeking a peaceful, well-equipped home—just ensure you cross-check every sales claim

featured_reviews.review_text:
Do read before buying extremely disappointing and feels like a deliberate fraud. Misleading

False assurances: They verbally convinced me that my building would be ready by March 2026, but insisted on writing 2028 in the agreement, claiming the entire cluster of buildings would take that long. Their line was: “Don’t worry, your specific building will be ready by 2026, but we must mention 2028 on paper for the whole project.” This is how buyers are trapped — verbal promises vs. written reality.

Bank disbursement trap: ICICI Bank was convinced by Mayfair’s claim that the project was “80% completed” and released 90% of the loan amount. The shocking part is that buyers trust the bank’s scrutiny, assuming such a strong institution must have verified progress. In reality, banks rely only on builder‑issued certificates, not actual site inspections. Since November, the project has remained stuck at “80% completion” with no visible progress.

Unfinished yet expanding: The funniest and most frustrating part is that their existing buildings are not even complete, yet they are already starting new sites in the same location. Buyers don’t question this, and that silence is exactly how they get trapped.

Buyer deception: This is the biggest fraud — lure buyers with optimistic verbal timelines, get them to sign papers, and later hide behind the written agreement that pushes delivery years ahead.

I strongly caution anyone considering Mayfair projects: do not trust verbal commitments, rely only on the written agreement. Be vigilant with loan disbursements, because once banks release funds, you are left paying EMIs while waiting years for possession.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I am currently living here on rent in Vinay Unique Gardens, Ekta Parksville. The society environment is peaceful and no one disturbs you, so if you are someone who likes a quiet place to live, this can be a decent option.

The rent is also reasonable. A 1BHK usually costs around ₹9,000 to ₹10,000, which is quite affordable compared to many nearby areas.

However, there are several issues residents should know before deciding to buy or move here.

The clubhouse is not functioning, even though it is part of the amenities. The water supply completely depends on tankers, as there is no VVMC water connection, which can sometimes be inconvenient.

The society maintenance is around ₹2,800 to ₹3,000 per month, which feels a bit high considering the facilities. Also, power cuts happen almost daily for around 1 hour.

Another thing to note is that tenants are charged around ₹2,000–₹2,500 as shifting charges for lift usage when moving in.

Overall, it is a quiet and affordable place for tenants, but if you are planning to buy a flat here, make sure you check all these factors carefully before making a decision.
